Author: Rajesh Bindal
Bench: Rajesh Bindal
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No.1369/2025

[@ Slp [Crl.] No.15588/2023]
 Suman Ghorui & Ors. Appellant(s)

VERSUS  THE STATE OF WEST BENGAL & ANR. Respondent(s)
 O R D E R Leave granted.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellants submits that the matter has been previously resolved between the appellant No.1-husband, and the respondent No.2-wife, which is the reason why the respondent No.2 has not chosen to appear before this Court, despite service of notice.

Reason: In this case, the divorce has already been granted, and the subsequent proceedings initiated by respondent No.2 under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 were also dismissed in default.

opennyai_summary.decision:
The appellants seek quashing of the proceedings arising out of FIR No.131/2016 dated 25.06.2016,
for the offences punishable under Sections 406/354/376/498A/120B of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, registered with the P.S. Jorabagan, Kolkata, at the behest of respondent No.2.
Accordingly, the impugned judgment stands quashed and the proceedings against the appellants,
arising out of FIR No.131/2016 dated 25.06.2016 for the offences punishable under Sections 406/354/376/498A/120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, registered with the P.S. Jorabagan,
Kolkata stand quashed.
Appeal is allowed.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
The appeal stands allowed in terms of the signed order.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Learned counsel appearing for the appellants submits that the matter has been previously resolved between the appellant No.1-husband, and the respondent No.2-wife, which is the reason why the respondent No.2 has not chosen to appear before this Court, despite service of notice.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Reason: In this case, the divorce has already been granted, and the subsequent proceedings initiated by respondent No.2 under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 were also dismissed in default.
Even on merits, we are of the considered view that the proceedings require to be quashed, as continuation of the proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.
